title: Data Validation for ML Pipelines
description: Schema and distribution assertions run on every batch before it reaches training — TFDV schema inference and Great Expectations suites catching null-rate spikes, unseen categorical values, and silently rescaled units before they become a quietly worse model.
viz: synthetic batch generator with sliders for null rate, unseen-category share, and mean shift, running a live expectation suite that marks each assertion pass/fail and shows which rows get quarantined versus which failures reject the whole batch

title: Dataset Versioning
description: Content-addressed dataset snapshots (DVC-style pointers, table-format time travel) so a training run can be replayed against the exact rows it saw, and why treating the query as the version breaks the moment a late-arriving row lands.
viz: commit timeline where each training run pins a dataset hash, with a toggle between pinning a snapshot and re-running the query showing the run reproduce exactly versus drift as late-arriving rows are appended, plus a row-count and checksum diff readout

title: Reproducible Feature Engineering Pipelines
description: One transformation definition shared by the batch and online paths, with fitted statistics (means, encoders, bucket edges) persisted as artifacts instead of recomputed — the fix for the classic bug where the serving path re-fits a scaler on live traffic.
viz: pipeline graph of fit and transform stages with a toggle between fitting at serving time and loading persisted statistics, showing the scaled feature value diverge between train and serve as a live-traffic distribution slider is moved

title: Feature Stores
description: An offline store for training and an online store for low-latency lookup behind a single feature definition — materialization jobs, TTLs, and entity keys — plus the honest question of when a feature store is over-engineering versus a plain cache plus a shared library.
viz: architecture panel with a feature-definition editor driving both stores, where a materialization-interval slider shows the online value going stale relative to offline and a latency readout compares an online-store hit against recomputing the feature inline

title: Online and Offline Feature Parity
description: Detecting the divergence between the feature values a model trained on and the ones it sees at inference by logging served features back to the offline store and running a scheduled parity job on the overlap — the failure that never raises an exception.
viz: parity job over logged serving features versus backfilled offline features with injectable mismatch sources (stale cache, different null fill, timezone shift), computing per-feature mismatch rate and flagging which features cross the alert threshold

title: Point-in-Time Correct Feature Joins
description: Joining labels to the feature values as of the label's event time rather than the latest value — the as-of join and its watermark and TTL edge cases that keep future information from leaking into training and inflating offline AUC.
viz: event timeline of feature updates and label events with a draggable label timestamp, where an as-of-join toggle shows the correct historical value versus the naive latest-value join and quantifies the leakage as an inflated offline accuracy number

title: Training-Serving Skew
description: The three sources of skew — divergent transformation code, divergent data (training on a filtered sample), and feedback-loop skew from the model's own predictions — and how each shows up as offline metrics that do not survive contact with production.
viz: side-by-side train and serve pipelines with individually injectable skew sources (code divergence, sampling filter, feedback loop), plotting the resulting feature-distribution gap and the corresponding drop from offline to online accuracy

title: Experiment Tracking
description: Logging params, metrics, artifacts, and the git SHA per run so a result can be found and rebuilt months later — MLflow and W&B run hierarchies, nested sweeps, and why an untracked notebook run is not a result.
viz: run table you populate by launching simulated training runs with different hyperparameters, with sortable metric columns, a parallel-coordinates plot over the parameter space, and a reproduce-run action that reports which runs logged enough metadata to rebuild

title: ML Pipeline Orchestration
description: DAG-based orchestration of ingest, validate, train, evaluate, and register steps in Airflow, Dagster, or Kubeflow — retries, idempotent task boundaries, backfills, and the sensors that stop a stalled upstream from silently training on stale data.
viz: interactive DAG where you fail individual tasks and watch retry policy, downstream skipping, and backfill re-runs play out, plus a schedule-interval control that demonstrates overlapping runs and the catch-up storm an unset max-active-runs produces

title: Model Registry and Stage Promotion
description: Immutable model versions with stage transitions (staging, production, archived), the metadata that must ride along (training dataset hash, metrics, input signature), and why serving resolves a registry alias rather than a filesystem path.
viz: registry table of model versions with promote and rollback buttons moving versions between stages, a serving pane resolving the production alias to whichever version currently holds it, and a broken-lineage flag on versions missing a dataset hash or signature

title: Offline Evaluation Gates
description: Automated promotion gates comparing a candidate against the incumbent on holdout and on named slices, with minimum-improvement and no-regression thresholds — and why a single aggregate metric happily promotes a model that is broken for one segment.
viz: gate configuration with thresholds for overall lift, per-slice regression tolerance, and minimum slice support, evaluated live against candidate versus baseline metrics so you can find the threshold settings that let a slice-regressing model through

title: Batch, Online, and Streaming Inference
description: Precomputed batch scoring, request-time online inference, and streaming scoring off an event log — chosen by feature freshness requirements, prediction cardinality, and latency budget rather than by preference, and the point where batch precompute stops being possible.
viz: workload configurator with request-rate, feature-freshness, and candidate-set-size controls that scores all three architectures on cost, prediction staleness, and p99 latency, showing batch precompute become infeasible as the input space grows

title: Serving Latency Budgets
description: Decomposing an end-to-end p99 budget across feature lookup, model forward pass, and network hops — why the p99 of the whole is not the sum of the p99s, and how a fan-out to N parallel feature lookups lets the tail dominate.
viz: budget allocator with per-stage latency distributions for feature lookup, inference, and post-processing, sampling thousands of requests to compute end-to-end p50 and p99 and showing the tail amplify as the number of parallel feature fetches rises

title: Shadow Deployment
description: Mirroring live traffic to a candidate model whose predictions are logged but never served — what it catches (latency regressions, feature-pipeline breakage, prediction-distribution shift) and the whole class of effects it cannot measure because nothing acts on the prediction.
viz: traffic mirror with an adjustable mirror percentage sending requests to both models, accumulating paired predictions into an agreement matrix and a latency comparison, with a toggle spelling out why business metrics stay unmeasurable in shadow mode

title: Canary Rollout for Models
description: Ramping a new model version through traffic percentages with automated analysis at each step — guardrail metrics, minimum sample size per stage, and the auto-rollback rule that has to fire before a bad model reaches full traffic.
viz: traffic-split ramp through 1, 5, 25, and 100 percent with injectable error-rate and latency regressions in the canary, computing per-stage significance against the baseline and firing an automatic rollback the moment a guardrail breaches

title: Champion-Challenger Promotion
description: Running a challenger continuously against the production champion on the same traffic and promoting only on a sustained win — how it differs from a one-shot canary, and the selection bias from judging a challenger on traffic the champion itself shaped.
viz: long-running comparison where champion and challenger accumulate scored traffic, with promotion-rule controls for sustained-win duration and required margin, plus a feedback-loop toggle showing the challenger's estimate biased by the champion's own routing

title: A/B Testing Models in Production
description: Randomizing users rather than requests into model variants, sizing the test for power on the business metric, and the traps that flip a verdict: peeking, interference between users, and novelty effects that decay by week two.
viz: experiment simulator with traffic-split, true-effect-size, and metric-variance controls running sequential p-value tracking that flags the peeking false positive, plus a novelty-decay toggle that makes an early significant win regress to nothing

title: Production Model Monitoring and Alerting
description: The four layers worth instrumenting — system health, input data quality, prediction distribution, and model quality once labels land — plus alert thresholds tuned so that drift pages a human only when it is actionable.
viz: dashboard streaming synthetic production traffic across all four monitoring layers with per-layer alert thresholds, where a noise slider makes the alert-fatigue tradeoff explicit as tighter thresholds turn benign fluctuation into pages

title: Data Drift vs Concept Drift
description: Input distribution shift in P(X) versus a changed relationship P(y|X) — why data drift is often harmless while concept drift always costs accuracy, and why only the first is detectable before labels arrive.
viz: 2D feature scatter with independent controls for shifting the input distribution and rotating the true decision boundary, showing an input-side detector fire on data drift while accuracy holds, then accuracy collapse under concept drift with no input-side signal at all

title: Population Stability Index
description: PSI as the binned symmetric divergence between a reference and a current distribution, the 0.1 and 0.25 rules of thumb, and the binning and sample-size choices that make it fire on noise or miss a real shift entirely.
viz: reference and current histograms with shift and spread controls plus a bin-count slider, computing per-bin and total PSI live, showing the score cross 0.1 and 0.25 and how coarse bins hide a shift that finer bins detect

title: KS Test vs KL Divergence
description: Two different questions asked of the same two samples: the Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic as the maximum CDF gap with a p-value that shrinks with sample size, versus KL divergence as an unbounded asymmetric information measure that needs smoothing when a bin goes empty.
viz: draggable reference and current distributions rendering both CDFs with the KS D-statistic marked as the largest vertical gap, alongside live KL and JS divergence readouts and a sample-size slider showing KS declare trivial shifts significant at scale

title: Online Drift Detection with ADWIN
description: Sequential detectors that flag change without a fixed reference window — ADWIN shrinking its adaptive window when two sub-windows differ, and DDM or Page-Hinkley on an error stream — for when a nightly batch PSI job reacts far too slowly.
viz: streaming metric with an injectable abrupt or gradual change point running ADWIN's window-splitting test live to show the window cut and the detection delay, with a confidence-parameter slider trading false alarms against how long gradual drift goes unnoticed

title: Label Lag and Delayed Ground Truth
description: When labels arrive days later or never — fraud chargebacks, churn, loan default — true model quality is unmeasurable exactly when it matters, so proxy metrics, label maturity curves, and the censoring bias of scoring only the labels that have landed carry the load.
viz: prediction stream with a configurable label-arrival delay distribution plotting measured accuracy over time against eventual true accuracy so the censored early estimate visibly misleads, plus a maturity-window control marking when a cohort is safe to evaluate

title: Retraining Triggers and Cadence
description: Scheduled versus triggered retraining — drift thresholds, performance-degradation triggers, and data-volume triggers — plus the cost of retraining too eagerly: prediction churn, unstable explanations, and a feedback loop that trains on the previous model's own output.
viz: months-long simulation over drifting data comparing fixed-cadence against threshold-triggered retraining, with drift-rate, retraining-cost, and trigger-threshold sliders plotting accumulated accuracy loss against retraining spend

title: Model Governance and Lineage
description: The provenance chain a regulated deployment must be able to answer for — which data, code, and hyperparameters produced this prediction — plus approval workflows, model cards, and retaining the artifacts needed to reproduce a decision months after it was made.
viz: clickable lineage graph tracing a single served prediction back through model version, training run, dataset snapshot, and feature definitions, with a delete-this-source action showing exactly which downstream claims become unprovable

title: Slice-Based Fairness Monitoring
description: Tracking metrics per protected and business-critical segment instead of in aggregate — disparity ratios, the minimum slice support needed for a stable estimate, and the Simpson's-paradox case where the aggregate improves while every slice degrades.
viz: per-slice metric table computed from a synthetic population with adjustable slice sizes and per-slice error rates, showing the aggregate hold steady while a small slice collapses, with a disparity-ratio threshold flag and a minimum-support cutoff greying unstable slices

title: CI/CD for ML
description: Pipelines that test code, data, and model together — unit tests on transformations, schema contract tests, a training smoke run, and an evaluation gate — where the promoted artifact is an immutable model version rather than a freshly rebuilt image.
viz: pipeline runner where you commit a change to code, data, or config and watch which stages re-run and which cached artifacts are invalidated, with injectable failures at each gate showing precisely where a bad model gets stopped

title: GPU Serving and Autoscaling
description: Dynamic batching and concurrency limits to keep a GPU fed, why request-rate autoscaling misfires on GPU-bound inference when queue depth and batch occupancy are the real signals, and the cold-start cost of loading model weights onto a fresh node.
viz: GPU inference queue with request-rate, max-batch-size, and batch-wait-timeout sliders computing throughput, utilization, and p99 latency live, plus an autoscaling panel racing rate-based against queue-depth-based scaling through a traffic spike with cold-start delay

title: Incident Response for ML Systems
description: Why an ML incident often has no error rate to page on, the runbook ordering that rolls back to the last known-good version before diagnosing, and the distinct root causes to separate: upstream schema change, feature-pipeline failure, drift, and a bad promotion.
viz: triage tree seeded with a symptom (shifted prediction distribution, latency spike, silent accuracy drop) that walks through feature-freshness, upstream-schema, model-version, and traffic-mix checks to narrow to a root cause, with a running time-to-mitigate counter

title: Cost Management for ML Infrastructure
description: Where ML spend actually goes — idle GPUs, repeated feature backfills, and always-on endpoints for low-traffic models — and the levers against it: spot instances with checkpointing, multi-model endpoints, quantization, and scale-to-zero for bursty traffic.
viz: monthly cost model with GPU-type, utilization, traffic-pattern, and retraining-frequency controls breaking spend into training, serving, and storage, showing how spot-with-checkpointing and scale-to-zero move the total against an SLA-violation penalty
